answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut mandate combined with incumbent's refusal to reopen pricing makes renegotiation (memory_c4 precedent) unlikely to succeed. memory_c2 demonstrates that moving to a low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate operations. memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments can unlock volume pricing, but we lack negotiating leverage here. At 94% line utilization with 14 days to contract expiration and no auto-renewal, deferring carries unacceptable delivery risk. Adding a second source (memory_c3) doesn't solve the primary cost mandate. Switching vendors aligns with the historical success in memory_c2 and offers the only path to meet the 18% reduction requirement. The primary risk is onboarding execution and potential service disruption during transition, but this is preferable to contract lapse or unmanageable cost structure. A standard experiment approach allows phased validation before full cutover.
